title: You need to be delusional if you want to succeed.

sentences.en: I want you to tell me if any of these sound like you.
sentences.zh: 我想让你告诉我，下面这些情况有没有哪一条听起来像你。

sentences.en: One, you feel like you've been lied to about what a good life looks like.
sentences.zh: 第一，你觉得自己被欺骗了，关于美好生活应该是什么样子。

sentences.en: You're pursuing a goal that sounds nice when you mention it at dinner with grandma, or a goal that wouldn't make your parents think you're a disappointment, and you really don't see it going anywhere.
sentences.zh: 你在追求一个目标，这个目标在跟奶奶吃饭时提起来很好听，或者是一个不会让你父母觉得你是个失败者的目标，而你其实根本看不到它有什么前途。

sentences.en: If you ignore that feeling, you wake up 10 years later with a degree, a decent job, and a never-ending sense of despair that you'll never be able to chase your own dreams.
sentences.zh: 如果你忽略那种感觉，十年后你会醒来，拿着一个学位，有一份体面的工作，以及一种永无止境的绝望感，觉得自己永远没法去追逐自己的梦想。

sentences.en: Two, you're productive, but not actually making progress toward anything.
sentences.zh: 第二，你很高效，但实际上没有朝着任何方向取得进展。

sentences.en: You wake up early, you listen to podcasts, you journal, you lift, your calendar is full, but you don't really know where you're going.
sentences.zh: 你早起，听播客，写日记，举铁，日程排得满满当当，但你并不真正知道自己要去哪里。

sentences.en: Give it five years and you'll still be figuring out what to do with your life.
sentences.zh: 再过五年，你依然在琢磨自己的人生该做什么。

sentences.en: Three, you're ambitious, but stay quiet because it sounds embarrassing to your friends and family.
sentences.zh: 第三，你很有野心，但保持沉默，因为在朋友和家人面前说出来会显得很尴尬。

sentences.en: You want a unique life, you don't want to fit in.
sentences.zh: 你想要一个独特的人生，你不想随大流。

sentences.en: But when people ask about your future, you water it down so nobody laughs at it.
sentences.zh: 但当别人问起你的未来时，你会把它说得轻描淡写，这样没人会嘲笑它。

sentences.en: You get stuck performing mental masturbation.
sentences.zh: 你被困在精神自慰里。

sentences.en: You feel special for wanting to be unique, but you still do the same thing as everyone else.
sentences.zh: 你因为想要与众不同而觉得自己很特别，但你仍然做着和其他人一样的事。

sentences.en: Nobody wants to end up in any of those three situations.
sentences.zh: 没人想落入这三种情况中的任何一种。

sentences.en: This video will change that for you.
sentences.zh: 这个视频会为你改变这一点。

sentences.en: Because one of my favorite things to do, it seems like a stupid past time, but I love to study the habits, actions, and thought processes of both successful people and mediocre people.
sentences.zh: 因为我最喜欢做的一件事，看起来像个愚蠢的消遣，但我喜欢研究成功者和平庸者双方的习惯、行为和思维过程。

sentences.en: And that's all success really is, is doing less of what the mediocre people do and doing more of what the successful people do.
sentences.zh: 而成功的全部真谛，就是少做平庸者做的事，多做成功者做的事。

sentences.en: In the next few videos on this channel will actually be dedicated to all of that.
sentences.zh: 这个频道接下来的几个视频，实际上会全部围绕这些展开。

sentences.en: This is just the first one.
sentences.zh: 这只是第一个。

sentences.en: So when we reverse engineer the habits, actions, and thoughts of people who have done the impossible like Elon Musk or Steve Jobs and any of the other greatest creatives, thinkers, and builders of the past, there is one pattern I've noticed between them all.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们逆向拆解那些完成不可能之事的人的习惯、行为和思维时，比如 Elon Musk 或 Steve Jobs，以及过去任何其他最伟大的创造者、思想家和建设者，我注意到他们之间有一个共同模式。

sentences.en: Their goals are delusional.
sentences.zh: 他们的目标是妄想的。

sentences.en: That's the key to their success.
sentences.zh: 那是他们成功的关键。

sentences.en: And that's exactly what we're going to go over.
sentences.zh: 而这正是我们要深入探讨的。

sentences.en: First, why average goals lead to mediocrity and failure, the psychology of delusional goals and why they work and why you need them, how to enter the same reality as ultra successful people, and of course how to achieve what most people think is impossible.
sentences.zh: 首先，为什么平庸的目标会导致平庸和失败，妄想目标背后的心理学原理，以及它们为什么有效、你为什么需要它们，如何进入和超级成功者相同的现实，当然还有如何实现大多数人认为不可能的事。

sentences.en: So that's what we're going to start with.
sentences.zh: 所以我们就从这里开始。

sentences.en: Why realistic goals lead to failure and mediocrity.
sentences.zh: 为什么现实的目标会导致失败和平庸。

sentences.en: And you fall into this category by default.
sentences.zh: 而你默认就属于这一类。

sentences.en: Everyone falls into this category by default.
sentences.zh: 每个人默认都掉进这一类。

sentences.en: And I think it's best illustrated by an Elon Musk quote.
sentences.zh: 我认为 Elon Musk 的一句话最能说明这一点。

sentences.en: "The most common error of a smart engineer is to optimize a thing that should not exist." So you have goals, even if you didn't set them.
sentences.zh: “一个聪明工程师最常犯的错误，是去优化一个本不该存在的东西。”所以你有目标，即使你没有主动设定它们。

sentences.en: That's just how the mind works.
sentences.zh: 大脑就是这么运作的。

sentences.en: And if you become aware of this or understand how your mind works, you can quickly see why you or other people aren't able to stick to the goals that they set.
sentences.zh: 如果你意识到这一点，或者理解了你的大脑是如何运作的，你很快就能明白为什么你或其他人无法坚持自己设定的目标。

sentences.en: And we're not talking about some New Year's resolution or some shallow goal that you set because you looked in the mirror and felt bad about yourself.
sentences.zh: 我们不是在说某个新年决心，或者某个肤浅的目标，你设定它只是因为照镜子时对自己感觉不好。

sentences.en: So you wanted to go to the gym or start eating healthy and you eat one healthy meal and then you quit immediately because you just forgot about it.
sentences.zh: 于是你想去健身房或者开始健康饮食，你吃了一顿健康餐，然后立刻就放弃了，因为你直接把它忘了。

sentences.en: Something more important stole your attention like something funny on your phone.
sentences.zh: 某个更重要的东西偷走了你的注意力，比如手机上某个好笑的东西。

sentences.en: Or in other words, because another unconscious goal was more important than the one you set and you're just not aware of it.
sentences.zh: 或者换句话说，因为另一个无意识的目标，比你设定的那个更重要，而你根本没意识到它的存在。

sentences.en: And that unconscious goal is usually convenience and comfort.
sentences.zh: 那个无意识的目标，通常就是便利和舒适。

sentences.en: That's what you want.
sentences.zh: 那才是你真正想要的。

sentences.en: Or you just don't want to draw attention to yourself.
sentences.zh: 或者你只是不想引起别人注意。

sentences.en: So you stop eating healthy or going to the gym because secretly and even without admitting to yourself, you don't want to stand out.
sentences.zh: 所以你不再健康饮食，也不去健身房了，因为你私下里、甚至对自己都不愿承认的是，你不想太出众。

sentences.en: So we're not talking about those kinds of goals.
sentences.zh: 所以我们谈的不是那类目标。

sentences.en: We're talking about how your mind is like a heat seeking missile.
sentences.zh: 我们谈的是，你的大脑就像一枚热追踪导弹。

sentences.en: Every thought you have and every action you take is aiming toward a goal.
sentences.zh: 你的每一个念头、每一个行动，都在瞄准一个目标。

sentences.en: It just makes sense, right?
sentences.zh: 这很合理，对吧？

sentences.en: I'm looking toward this camera because I have the goal of creating a video.
sentences.zh: 我看着这个摄像头，是因为我有一个拍视频的目标。

sentences.en: I may be tapping my foot because I have the goal of just not being bored.
sentences.zh: 我可能在抖脚，是因为我有一个不想无聊的目标。

sentences.en: It's every single little thing.
sentences.zh: 每一件小事都是如此。

sentences.en: Everything is goal directed or directed by stimuli, which we'll talk about in a second.
sentences.zh: 一切都是由目标驱动的，或者由刺激驱动的，这个我们马上会讲。

sentences.en: But you have to understand that your mind is optimizing for a goal that you probably never chose and that you don't even know is there.
sentences.zh: 但你必须明白，你的大脑正在为一个你很可能从未选择过、甚至不知道它存在的目标做优化。

sentences.en: Or someone else assigned you the goal like go to school, get a job, retire at 65 because that's what you were raised to do.
sentences.zh: 或者是别人给你指派了目标，比如上学、找工作、65岁退休，因为你从小就被这么养大。

sentences.en: That's what you were conditioned to do and you never questioned it.
sentences.zh: 你被这么规训，而且你从未质疑过。

sentences.en: And so those sit in the back of your head and silently guide every action that you take without you realizing it.
sentences.zh: 于是这些目标就待在你的脑海深处，在你毫无察觉的情况下，默默引导着你的一举一动。

sentences.en: So I want you to actually take a second and think about that because this is massive.
sentences.zh: 所以我希望你真正花点时间想一想，因为这太重要了。

sentences.en: This could mean that the entire direction of your life and where you end up in life is completely out of your control or at least out of your awareness.
sentences.zh: 这可能意味着，你人生的整个方向、以及你最终的归宿，完全不在你的掌控之中，至少不在你的觉知之内。

sentences.en: Every single thing you think or do is aiming toward a goal.
sentences.zh: 你思考或做的每一件事，都在瞄准一个目标。

sentences.en: Do not forget about that.
sentences.zh: 别忘了这一点。

sentences.en: So here's how it goes.
sentences.zh: 事情是这样的。

sentences.en: First you're born.
sentences.zh: 首先，你出生了。

sentences.en: Your first goal is survival.
sentences.zh: 你的第一个目标是生存。

sentences.en: And then your parents have been thinking about what goals they want you to pursue for quite some time now.
sentences.zh: 然后，你的父母已经琢磨了相当长一段时间，他们想让你追求什么目标。

sentences.en: They want what's best for you so to say but really they want what's best for them.
sentences.zh: 他们想要给你最好的，话是这么说，但实际上，他们想要的是对他们自己最好的。

sentences.en: They want you to be a respectable young adult that doesn't embarrass them.
sentences.zh: 他们希望你成为一个体面的年轻人，别给他们丢脸。

sentences.en: And then your parents teach you how to walk, how to communicate and then eventually what their version of success for you looks like.
sentences.zh: 然后你的父母教你走路、教你沟通，最终教你他们眼中你该有的成功版本。

sentences.en: Which is usually the goals that society passed down to them unless your parents questioned them or your parents were high agency.
sentences.zh: 这通常是社会传递给他们的目标，除非你的父母质疑过这些，或者你的父母是那种高自主性的人。

sentences.en: So go to school, get a job, praise your God.
sentences.zh: 所以，上学、找工作、赞美你的上帝。

sentences.en: And so that's what you do.
sentences.zh: 于是你就这么做了。

sentences.en: You go to school and then you go to college because that's just what's next.
sentences.zh: 你去上学，然后去上大学，因为这就是下一步该做的事。

sentences.en: You don't really make that decision.
sentences.zh: 你并没有真正做出那个决定。

sentences.en: That's the only decision you can make.
sentences.zh: 那是你唯一能做的决定。

sentences.en: And then you get the job, you hit the milestones and you check the boxes.
sentences.zh: 然后你找到了工作，达成了里程碑，打完了该打的勾。

sentences.en: And then after almost a quarter of your life you start to wonder if this was what you wanted in the first place, which is kind of not cool.
sentences.zh: 然后在将近四分之一的人生过去之后，你开始怀疑这到底是不是你最初想要的，这感觉挺糟的。

sentences.en: A quarter of your life is gone.
sentences.zh: 四分之一的人生就这么没了。

sentences.en: And so the default state is having average goals and just going with the flow.
sentences.zh: 所以默认状态就是拥有一些平庸的目标，随波逐流。

sentences.en: And if you understand entropy, you understand how disastrous this can be.
sentences.zh: 如果你理解熵是什么，你就知道这会有多灾难。

sentences.en: And entropy illustrates that systems trend toward disorder.
sentences.zh: 熵揭示了一个规律：系统会趋向混乱。

sentences.en: Now applied to the mind, psychic entropy, psychic isn't some fancy word like you're moving water bottles with your mind.
sentences.zh: 应用到心智上，就是心理熵。psychic 不是什么花哨的词，不是说你用意念移动水瓶。

sentences.en: It literally just means of the mind.
sentences.zh: 它字面意思就是“心智的”。

sentences.en: It's the mind.
sentences.zh: 就是心智。

sentences.en: So psychic entropy means that your mind and therefore your life drifts toward disorder and chaos.
sentences.zh: 所以心理熵意味着你的心智、进而你的人生，会漂向混乱和无序。

sentences.en: And you can see this everywhere.
sentences.zh: 你到处都能看到这个现象。

sentences.en: This is just what happens if you don't water a plant, it dies.
sentences.zh: 你不给植物浇水，它就会死，这就是自然规律。

sentences.en: If you don't clean your room, it slowly gets more disorganized with time.
sentences.zh: 你不打扫房间，它就会随着时间变得越来越乱。

sentences.en: If you don't maintain habits of personal development, your mind slowly devolves into chaos.
sentences.zh: 你不维持个人成长的习惯，你的心智就会慢慢退化成一片混乱。

sentences.en: And so this is what happens on the default path is you have these average goals that you didn't choose, that you didn't set.
sentences.zh: 这就是默认路径上会发生的事：你拥有这些平庸的目标，不是你选的，不是你定的。

sentences.en: You don't put any effort into them because you don't actually care about them.
sentences.zh: 你不会为它们付出任何努力，因为你根本不在乎它们。

sentences.en: And then you eventually find yourself in a rut.
sentences.zh: 然后你最终发现自己陷入了一潭死水。

sentences.en: Everyone experiences that.
sentences.zh: 每个人都经历过。

sentences.en: That's why this is such an evergreen video.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么这个视频永远不过时。

sentences.en: This shouldn't be a thing like you should want better for yourself.
sentences.zh: 这本不该是个问题，你应该对自己有更高的要求。

sentences.en: But that's also just the nature of reality.
sentences.zh: 但这也是现实的本质。

sentences.en: And I do think it's there for a reason, because at some point, a system becomes unstable and a new, more ordered structure must emerge.
sentences.zh: 而且我确实认为它的存在是有原因的，因为在某个时刻，一个系统会变得不稳定，然后一个更有序的新结构必须涌现出来。

sentences.en: So when you think of water that is just pouring out of a faucet, let's say into a bathtub, eventually it gets so chaotic that a whirlpool starts to form a beautiful ordered whirlpool.
sentences.zh: 想象一下水从水龙头流出来，流进浴缸，最终它会变得如此混乱，以至于一个漩涡开始形成——一个美丽的、有序的漩涡。

sentences.en: So in your life, you hit a point where the lower part of you wants to stay the same and the higher part wants something more.
sentences.zh: 所以在你的生命中，你会到达一个点：那个低层次的你想要保持不变，而那个高层次的你渴望更多。

sentences.en: And it feels like you're being ripped in half.
sentences.zh: 那种感觉就像你被撕成了两半。

sentences.en: That is a signal to completely turn your life around.
sentences.zh: 那是一个信号，一个让你彻底扭转人生的信号。

sentences.en: That's what my next newsletter is actually going to be about, is kind of how to launch out of a very bad position in your life, because that's the best time to do it.
sentences.zh: 这其实也是我下一篇 newsletter 要讲的内容，就是如何从一个非常糟糕的人生处境中弹射起步，因为那正是做这件事的最佳时机。

sentences.en: So the reason most average and realistic goals lead to mediocrity and failure is because of how you choose them.
sentences.zh: 大多数平庸、现实的目标之所以导致平庸和失败，原因在于你选择它们的方式。

sentences.en: First, you look at what you think is possible or what you know is possible and what you know at this point in your life is really only told to you by your parents or your teachers or what other average people do.
sentences.zh: 首先，你去看那些你认为可能、或者你知道可能的事情，而你在人生这个阶段所知道的事情，其实只是你的父母、老师或者其他平庸的人告诉你的。

sentences.en: And then from those possible goals, you water it down a bit so that people won't laugh at you for trying to improve yourself because whenever you try to improve yourself, crabs in the bucket mentality, all of your friends are gonna be like,
sentences.zh: 然后从那些可能的目标里，你再把它打点折扣，这样别人就不会因为你试图提升自己而嘲笑你。因为每当你试图提升自己，桶里的螃蟹心态就来了，你所有的朋友都会说：

sentences.en: Oh, you should drink this beer.
sentences.zh: 哦，你应该喝这杯啤酒。

sentences.en: You shouldn't stick to your health goals.
sentences.zh: 你不该死守你的健康目标。

sentences.en: Like Oh, come on, just lighten up, live a little bit.
sentences.zh: 哎呀，别这样，放轻松点，享受一下生活嘛。

sentences.en: And so you want to avoid that because you know it's going to happen.
sentences.zh: 于是你就想避开这些，因为你知道它一定会发生。

sentences.en: So you water down the goals and don't take them seriously in the first place.
sentences.zh: 所以你一开始就把目标稀释了，根本没把它们当回事。

sentences.en: And a goal only feels realistic if it fits the life that your parents, teachers and friends already expected you to have.
sentences.zh: 一个目标只有符合父母、老师、朋友早就为你预设好的人生，才会让人觉得"现实"。

sentences.en: In other words, your mind is a cage.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，你的大脑是一座牢笼。

sentences.en: And if you keep choosing to live in that cage, you'll never have the chance to notice a potentially life changing opportunity.
sentences.zh: 如果你一直选择活在那座牢笼里，你永远没机会注意到那些可能改变一生的机会。

sentences.en: That's what a lot of this video is about is about noticing.
sentences.zh: 这期视频很大一部分内容，讲的就是"注意到"。

sentences.en: And if you don't notice that opportunity, there's no way you can act on it.
sentences.zh: 如果你没注意到那个机会，你根本不可能去行动。

sentences.en: And again, your life just slowly gets worse and worse and worse until the pain becomes great, that you either get crushed or you finally decide to act on it.
sentences.zh: 然后你的人生就只会越来越糟、越来越糟，直到痛苦大到要么把你压垮，要么你终于决定行动。

sentences.en: So delusional goals.
sentences.zh: 所以，妄想型目标。

sentences.en: What are they?
sentences.zh: 它们是什么？

sentences.en: Why do they matter?
sentences.zh: 它们为什么重要？

sentences.en: Are they actually delusional?
sentences.zh: 它们真的算妄想吗？

sentences.en: We'll start with a quote to transition from Maxwell Maltz.
sentences.zh: 我们先引用 Maxwell Maltz 的一句话来过渡。

sentences.en: The man who conceives himself to be a failure type person will find some way to fail in spite of all his good intentions or willpower, even if the opportunity is literally dumped in his lap.
sentences.zh: 一个自认为是失败者的人，不管有多少善意或意志力，总会找到办法失败，哪怕机会就明晃晃地掉在他腿上。

sentences.en: The person who conceives himself to be a victim of injustice, one who was meant to suffer will invariably find circumstances to verify his opinions.
sentences.zh: 一个自认为是不公受害者、注定要受苦的人，总会找到环境来验证他的看法。

sentences.en: Now, another thing I like to think about is why humans are unique or why humans are different from animals and humans.
sentences.zh: 另外，我经常思考的一个问题是：人类为什么独特？人类和动物到底有什么不同？

sentences.en: They're not unique in the sense that they have memory or a different type of consciousness than animals or a more refined intelligence than animals, even though those play a role.
sentences.zh: 人类的独特之处不在于有记忆，也不在于有和动物不同的意识类型，或者比动物更精密的智力，尽管这些确实起了一定作用。

sentences.en: They're unique because they constantly simulate the future to steer the present.
sentences.zh: 人类的独特之处在于，他们不断模拟未来，以此来驾驭当下。

sentences.en: You think about the future more than you do the past, because usually you aren't really thinking about the past.
sentences.zh: 你思考未来的时间比思考过去多得多，因为你通常并不真的在想过去。

sentences.en: The future is what causes your present behavior.
sentences.zh: 是未来在驱动你当下的行为。

sentences.en: Again, all behavior is mostly goal directed.
sentences.zh: 再说一遍，所有行为本质上都是目标导向的。

sentences.en: So contrary to, I guess, popular belief is your actions do not create the future.
sentences.zh: 所以，跟主流看法相反：你的行动并不创造未来。

sentences.en: You create the future first and your actions follow.
sentences.zh: 你先创造未来，然后行动才会跟上。

sentences.en: So all of this falls under the umbrella of selective attention, meaning your brain either gets pulled by stimuli or directed by a goal.
sentences.zh: 这一切都归在"选择性注意力"这个范畴里，意思是你的大脑要么被刺激牵着走，要么被目标指引。

sentences.en: And when you focus on one thing, that means by definition, you're not focused on the 99.99 percent of other things you could be focusing on.
sentences.zh: 当你专注于一件事时，从定义上说，你就没有在关注那 99.99% 你本可以关注的其他事情。

sentences.en: Your attention is goal directed rather than tossed around like a ragdoll looking for the next cheap dopamine hit.
sentences.zh: 你的注意力是目标导向的，而不是像个破布娃娃一样被扔来扔去，四处寻找下一次廉价的多巴胺快感。

sentences.en: That's the important part because delusional goals force this.
sentences.zh: 这才是关键，因为妄想型目标会迫使你做到这一点。

sentences.en: If you're focused on one overarching delusional goal and only focused on that thing, then everything else is noise.
sentences.zh: 如果你只专注于一个压倒一切的妄想型目标，只关注那一件事，那其他一切都是噪音。

sentences.en: So I want you to imagine two different people with drastically different goals.
sentences.zh: 所以我想让你想象两个目标截然不同的人。

sentences.en: Person one, Tommy, has the same goal as almost everyone else.
sentences.zh: 第一个人，Tommy，他的目标和几乎所有人一样。

sentences.en: Go to school, get an education, get a decent job so he can finally afford a nice apartment and acquire enough material status symbols to attract a mate.
sentences.zh: 上学、拿文凭、找一份体面的工作，这样他就能终于租得起一套不错的公寓，攒够物质身份符号来吸引一个伴侣。

sentences.en: Person two, Johnny, has a goal that seems impossible.
sentences.zh: 第二个人，Johnny，他的目标看起来不可能实现。

sentences.en: Build a content business that makes 100K a month in six months as one example that I guess many in my audience can relate with.
sentences.zh: 六个月内打造一个每月收入 10 万美元的内容生意——举个例子，我猜很多观众都能感同身受。

sentences.en: Now will Tommy ever have the possibility of making more money than what a decent job would pay him?
sentences.zh: 现在我问你，Tommy 有没有可能赚到比一份"体面工作"更多的钱？

sentences.en: Will Tommy ever learn something outside of school that allows him to pursue a more lucrative opportunity?
sentences.zh: Tommy 有没有可能在学校之外学到什么东西，让他能去追求一个更赚钱的机会？

sentences.en: No, because that's not what his attention is selecting for.
sentences.zh: 不会，因为他的注意力根本没在筛选那些东西。

sentences.en: He could come across life changing information and his mind will consider it noise just because it's not necessary to achieve the goal he's pursuing.
sentences.zh: 他可能遇到能改变一生的信息，但他的大脑会把它当成噪音，只因为它对实现他正在追求的目标没用。

sentences.en: Johnny, on the other hand, cannot think like the average person.
sentences.zh: 而 Johnny 这边，他没法像普通人那样思考。

sentences.en: To achieve that delusional goal, he realizes that most actions he's taking are completely useless.
sentences.zh: 为了实现那个妄想级的目标，他意识到自己正在做的大多数行动完全没用。

sentences.en: So a properly set delusional goal pushes your brain into the unknown.
sentences.zh: 所以，一个设定得当的妄想目标会把你的大脑推进未知领域。

sentences.en: Everything you knew before is off the table, you can't use it.
sentences.zh: 你以前知道的一切都不作数了，你用不上它们。

sentences.en: And what this does is it accelerates neuroplasticity.
sentences.zh: 而这会加速神经可塑性。

sentences.en: Consistency reinforces pathways in your brain, but novelty and challenge stimulate learning and change faster.
sentences.zh: 持续重复会强化你大脑里的通路，但新奇和挑战能更快地刺激学习和改变。

sentences.en: So flipping the switch and going all in on a goal throws your brain into an environment where it has no choice but to rewire fast and the new behavior becomes your new baseline.
sentences.zh: 所以，按下开关、全力投入一个目标，会把你的大脑扔进一个环境里，它别无选择，只能快速重塑，而新行为会变成你的新基线。

sentences.en: And even better, many have experienced this in short bursts of their life is that this is when the five intrinsic drivers of flow and obsession come into play, which create a blissful quality of life.
sentences.zh: 更棒的是，很多在人生短暂爆发期经历过这个的人都知道，这时候心流和痴迷的五个内在驱动力就会开始起作用，它们会创造一种极乐的生活品质。

sentences.en: I mean, it's the flow state.
sentences.zh: 我是说，那就是心流状态。

sentences.en: It's the peak human experience.
sentences.zh: 那是人类的巅峰体验。

sentences.en: And those five drivers are one, curiosity, which is the desire to explore the unknown, learn how to change and fill knowledge gaps.
sentences.zh: 那五个驱动力是：第一，好奇心，也就是探索未知、学习如何改变、填补知识空白的欲望。

sentences.en: And this results in good dopamine from novelty and norepinephrine, which heightens attention preparing you to learn.
sentences.zh: 这会带来由新奇感产生的好多巴胺，以及去甲肾上腺素，它会提升注意力，让你准备好学习。

sentences.en: The second is passion.
sentences.zh: 第二是热情。

sentences.en: So an intense enthusiasm is built for the path that allows you to change your life.
sentences.zh: 你会对那条能改变你人生的道路建立起强烈的热忱。

sentences.en: This results in more good dopamine and norepinephrine.
sentences.zh: 这会产生更多的好多巴胺和去甲肾上腺素。

sentences.en: The next is purpose, which is the feeling that your actions contribute to something larger than yourself.
sentences.zh: 下一个是目的感，也就是感觉你的行动在为比自己更大的事做贡献。

sentences.en: Achieving goals results in more dopamine and reinforces behavior.
sentences.zh: 达成目标会产生更多多巴胺，并强化行为。

sentences.en: Serotonin stems from significance and belonging.
sentences.zh: 血清素来自重要感和归属感。

sentences.en: Oxytocin stems from connection.
sentences.zh: 催产素来自连接。

sentences.en: The next is autonomy, which is the desire to direct your own life and work, to control your choices, actions and environment, which results in yet again more dopamine and a reduction in cortisol, the stress from feeling put in a box, allowing for creative decision making.
sentences.zh: 下一个是自主性，也就是掌控自己人生和工作的欲望，掌控你的选择、行动和环境，这同样会产生更多多巴胺，并降低皮质醇，那种被框住带来的压力，从而允许创造性决策。

sentences.en: And then mastery, the process of learning and growing, is its own reward.
sentences.zh: 然后是精通，学习和成长的过程本身就是奖赏。

sentences.en: This results in sustainable good dopamine that keeps you in the game, keeps you playing.
sentences.zh: 这会产生可持续的好多巴胺，让你留在牌桌上，让你继续玩下去。

sentences.en: And so that's kind of what we're aiming for here is you throw yourself into the unknown, you become curious, and maybe you become curious before enough to throw yourself into the unknown, and then you generate passion, right?
sentences.zh: 所以这大概就是我们想要达到的状态：你把自己扔进未知，你变得好奇，也许你在把自己扔进未知之前就已经足够好奇了，然后你产生热情，对吧？

sentences.en: You're not passionate about things until you've invested time and energy into them.
sentences.zh: 在你投入时间和精力之前，你不可能对什么事情有热情。

sentences.en: You can't find your passion because you haven't done anything.
sentences.zh: 你找不到你的热情，因为你什么都没做过。

sentences.en: You have to stick it out into the unknown until you become passionate about something.
sentences.zh: 你必须在未知里坚持住，直到你对某件事产生热情。

sentences.en: And so many people get this wrong.
sentences.zh: 太多人把这点搞错了。

sentences.en: Like you don't have to be passionate about some fancy-pantsy artistic thing.
sentences.zh: 你不必对什么花里胡哨的艺术类东西有热情。

sentences.en: You can become passionate about literally anything.
sentences.zh: 你几乎可以对任何事情产生热情。

sentences.en: As long as you dive deep enough into it and learn enough about it so that you can kind of nerd out about it, that's where passion starts to come into play.
sentences.zh: 只要你钻研得足够深，学得足够多，多到你能对它如数家珍，那就是热情开始起作用的时候。

sentences.en: And then once you can tie that passion to a sense of purpose and eventually do your own thing with it, so autonomy and mastery, then that's the best way to live.
sentences.zh: 然后一旦你能把那份热情和一种目的感联系起来，并最终用它做你自己的事，也就是获得自主性和精通，那就是最好的生活方式。

sentences.en: That's what I'm all about with the things that I teach.
sentences.zh: 这就是我教的所有东西的核心。

sentences.en: And so this all sounds great, but I can hear your objection because I've faced the objection before myself.
sentences.zh: 所以这一切听起来都很棒，但我能听到你的反对意见，因为我自己也面对过这种反对。

sentences.en: And that objection is, "But Dan, I've tried setting a goal like this before, and I didn't feel any of this.
sentences.zh: 那个反对意见是："可是 Dan，我以前试过设定这样的目标，我完全没有感受到你说的这些东西。

sentences.en: I didn't feel motivated.
sentences.zh: 我一点动力都没有。

sentences.en: I just set the goal." And yes, that's exactly what we're trying to avoid.
sentences.zh: 我就是设了个目标而已。"没错，这正是我们要避免的。

sentences.en: Your goal needs gravity.
sentences.zh: 你的目标需要有引力。

sentences.en: It needs to pull you toward it.
sentences.zh: 它需要把你拉向它。

sentences.en: It needs to be so strong that everything else in your life just becomes stupid and pointless.
sentences.zh: 它需要强大到让你觉得生活中其他一切都变得愚蠢、毫无意义。

sentences.en: And that's difficult to do.
sentences.zh: 而这是很难做到的。

sentences.en: That's why this is going to be a video series rather than just one video.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么这会是一个系列视频，而不是一个视频就讲完。

sentences.en: So for now, we just have to learn how to properly set a delusional goal.
sentences.zh: 所以现在，我们只需要学会如何正确地设定一个妄念级目标。

sentences.en: And in reality, we're not setting a goal.
sentences.zh: 而实际上，我们不是在设定目标。

sentences.en: What we're doing is we're entering a new reality.
sentences.zh: 我们正在做的事情是进入一个新的现实。

sentences.en: And that sounds woo-woo.
sentences.zh: 这听起来很玄乎。

sentences.en: That sounds weird, but that's what you're doing.
sentences.zh: 听起来很奇怪，但你正在做的就是这件事。

sentences.en: And so we want to enter the same reality as ultra successful people.
sentences.zh: 我们想要进入的是和那些极度成功的人一样的现实。

sentences.en: And a quote that I love by Anthony D'Amelio is that, "Every great idea starts out as blasphemy.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢 Anthony D'Amelio 的一句话："每一个伟大的想法，一开始都是亵渎。

sentences.en: Everyone is going to think you're crazy because that idea scares them." And I think the best way of illustrating this is with Steve Jobs.
sentences.zh: 每个人都会觉得你疯了，因为那个想法让他们害怕。"我觉得说明这一点最好的例子就是 Steve Jobs。

sentences.en: So Steve Jobs would walk into a room, state an impossible deadline or an impossible product as if it were already decided.
sentences.zh: Steve Jobs 会走进一个房间，宣布一个不可能完成的截止日期或一个不可能实现的产品，就好像它已经板上钉钉了一样。

sentences.en: He'd say, "We'll ship it by January and it will do this with such total conviction that the room of engineers who knew it was impossible would leave believing it and then build toward it like it was simply the plan." This was Steve Jobs' reality distortion field.
sentences.zh: 他会说："我们一月之前发货，它会做到这些。"语气如此笃定，以至于满屋子知道这不可能的工程师离开时都信了，然后朝着它去构建，就好像这只是一个既定计划。这就是 Steve Jobs 的现实扭曲力场。

sentences.en: Most people would dismiss it as charisma or manipulation or him being an asshole when it was simply him re-aiming the room's attention.
sentences.zh: 大多数人会把它归结为个人魅力、操纵或者他是个混蛋，但实际上他只是在重新校准整个房间的注意力。

sentences.en: Steve Jobs refused to be pulled by the stimuli of "this timeline can't possibly work" and overrode it with a future target.
sentences.zh: Steve Jobs 拒绝被"这个时间线根本不可能"这类刺激牵着走，而是用一个未来的目标覆盖了它。

sentences.en: Every brain in the room started selecting for a path instead of selecting for reasons it wouldn't work.
sentences.zh: 房间里的每一个大脑都开始为一条路径做选择，而不是为它行不通的理由做选择。

sentences.en: And that's just the thing.
sentences.zh: 而这就是关键所在。

sentences.en: Most people have a misunderstanding of what a goal is.
sentences.zh: 大多数人对目标是什么有误解。

sentences.en: A goal is not a destination that you hit.
sentences.zh: 目标不是你到达的一个终点。

sentences.en: It's not climbing up the mountain and reaching the top.
sentences.zh: 不是爬上那座山然后登顶。

sentences.en: A goal is a point of view.
sentences.zh: 目标是一个视角。

sentences.en: Because when you're at the top of the mountain, now you have a completely different way of viewing everything underneath.
sentences.zh: 因为当你站在山顶的时候，你对下面的一切有了完全不同的看法。

sentences.en: It doesn't matter that you reach the top.
sentences.zh: 你是否到达山顶并不重要。

sentences.en: Like you're going to go home and go to bed the same as you do every night.
sentences.zh: 你还是要回家，像每天晚上一样上床睡觉。

sentences.en: It's just not that important.
sentences.zh: 它真的没那么重要。

sentences.en: But what you gained was a vantage point.
sentences.zh: 但你获得的是一个制高点。

sentences.en: You gained a new perspective.
sentences.zh: 你获得了一个新的视角。

sentences.en: So a goal is a filter that decides what your brain sees as important and what it sees as meaningless or unimportant.
sentences.zh: 所以目标是一个过滤器，它决定你的大脑把什么视为重要，把什么视为无意义或不重要。

sentences.en: So I hope that makes sense because that is just so powerful to understand that.
sentences.zh: 所以我希望你能理解这一点，因为明白这个道理真的太有力量了。

sentences.en: Is that you're not actually trying to reach the goal.
sentences.zh: 那就是：你其实并不是在试图"达到"那个目标。

sentences.en: That's the kind of self-help dogma that so many people are indoctrinated with.
sentences.zh: 这是很多人被灌输的那种自助类教条。

sentences.en: And then they go and turn against goals and say that goal setting is useless and all you need is systems.
sentences.zh: 然后他们反过来攻击目标，说设定目标没用，你只需要系统。

sentences.en: When a goal isn't meant to be hit, it's a point of view.
sentences.zh: 但目标本来就不是用来达成的，它是一个视角。

sentences.en: It's what filters information.
sentences.zh: 它是筛选信息的过滤器。

sentences.en: It's what allows you to notice opportunities because your attention and your focus is looking in a different direction from a different level.
sentences.zh: 它能让你注意到机会，因为你的注意力和焦点正从一个不同的层面、一个不同的方向去看。

sentences.en: In other words, you're in a different reality.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，你身处一个不同的现实。

sentences.en: You're seeing different things that other people aren't seeing.
sentences.zh: 你能看到别人看不到的东西。

sentences.en: So to properly set this delusional goal and create your own reality distortion field, here's what you need to do.
sentences.zh: 所以，要正确设定这个妄想级目标，创造你自己的现实扭曲力场，你需要做以下这些事。

sentences.en: And now would be a good time to pull out a notebook or open up Eden to take notes.
sentences.zh: 现在是个好时机，拿出笔记本或者打开 Eden 来做笔记。

sentences.en: But step one is to install the point of view.
sentences.zh: 第一步，是安装这个视角。

sentences.en: And there are exactly two things that you need to set a delusional goal.
sentences.zh: 设定一个妄想级目标，你只需要两样东西。

sentences.en: The first is that the goal has to be so big that you think it's impossible.
sentences.zh: 第一，这个目标必须大到你自己觉得不可能实现。

sentences.en: And second, you need to set a timeline so short you also think that's impossible.
sentences.zh: 第二，你需要设定一个短到你自己也觉得不可能实现的时间线。

sentences.en: So a goal that's impossible and a timeline that's impossible to hit because impossible is relative to your current situation.
sentences.zh: 所以，一个不可能的目标，加上一个不可能达成的时间线，因为"不可能"是相对于你当前处境而言的。

sentences.en: It actually is possible.
sentences.zh: 它实际上是可能的。

sentences.en: But if it were possible to you, then you wouldn't be operating in the unknown.
sentences.zh: 但如果对你来说是可能的，那你就不会在未知中行动了。

sentences.en: You wouldn't be doing anything new.
sentences.zh: 你就不会去做任何新的事情。

sentences.en: Now, if you don't know what goal to set or even what to do with your life, I find it helpful to just start with the most painful problem in your life that would unlock other areas of your life.
sentences.zh: 如果你不知道该设定什么目标，甚至不知道该拿你的人生做什么，我发现从一个最痛苦的问题开始很有用，一个能解锁你人生其他领域的问题。

sentences.en: That's like your main priority.
sentences.zh: 那就是你的首要任务。

sentences.en: So for most people, that usually revolves around fitness or finances because getting in the gym and dropping 20 pounds energy and mental health, making it easier to start turning your life around.
sentences.zh: 对大多数人来说，这通常围绕着健身或财务状况，因为走进健身房、减掉20磅，会带来精力和心理健康，让你更容易开始扭转人生。

sentences.en: This was true for me.
sentences.zh: 对我来说就是这样。

sentences.en: And it's true for a lot of business people that I talked to is that their gateway drug into business was fitness.
sentences.zh: 我聊过的很多商业人士也是如此：他们进入商业的入门毒品，是健身。

sentences.en: I was in the gym since I was like 14 or 15.
sentences.zh: 我从大概14、15岁就开始进健身房了。

sentences.en: I had a little garage gym, which was really just a bench press and a captain's chair.
sentences.zh: 我有一个小车库健身房，其实就是一个卧推架和一个罗马椅。

sentences.en: But I'd go out there because I just wanted veins in my arms.
sentences.zh: 但我会去那里练，因为我就是想让手臂上爆出血管。

sentences.en: It didn't matter how I started because I learned so much.
sentences.zh: 我怎么开始的并不重要，因为我学到了太多东西。

sentences.en: And I eventually fell in love with the process.
sentences.zh: 最终我爱上了这个过程。

sentences.en: And it taught me the habits and behaviors that transfer over so well to something like business.
sentences.zh: 它教会了我那些习惯和行为模式，而这些能非常好地迁移到商业这样的事情上。

sentences.en: And obviously, the energy and the confidence helped a lot with that.
sentences.zh: 而且很明显，精力和自信对做商业帮助巨大。

sentences.en: On the finances side of things, making more money relieves stress.
sentences.zh: 在财务方面，赚更多钱能缓解压力。

sentences.en: It opens your mind and it lets you invest in other areas of your life.
sentences.zh: 它能打开你的思维，让你有能力投资人生的其他领域。

sentences.en: And the specific how of achieving those goals doesn't need to happen yet because simply by setting the goal, if it's a real goal that is on your mind all the time, it's your main nor star that allows your mind to identify finally and learn the how.
sentences.zh: 而实现这些目标的具体方法，现在还不需要出现，因为仅仅通过设定目标，如果它是一个真正的目标，一个时刻在你脑海里的目标，它就是你的北极星，能让你的大脑最终识别并学会那个方法。

sentences.en: Because you don't know where to find it.
sentences.zh: 因为你根本不知道去哪里找。

sentences.en: Next, you need to ask yourself one question.
sentences.zh: 接下来，你需要问自己一个问题。

sentences.en: Is the goal and timeline you just set impossible for who you are now?
sentences.zh: 你刚刚设定的目标和时间线，对现在的你来说，是不是不可能完成？

sentences.en: In other words, can your current approach get you there?
sentences.zh: 换句话说，你现在的做法能让你到达那里吗？

sentences.en: If yes, the goal is linear, not impossible, reject it and raise it further.
sentences.zh: 如果能，那这个目标就是线性的，不是不可能，拒绝它，把它再拉高。

sentences.en: The goal must sit beyond your existing skills, habits and assumptions of what's possible, because that's exactly what creates a lens that shows you a new reality instead of a to do list.
sentences.zh: 目标必须超出你现有的技能、习惯和对可能性的假设，因为正是这一点，才能创造出一个让你看见新现实的透镜，而不是一张待办清单。

sentences.en: Now, last, the goal must be singular and self chosen.
sentences.zh: 最后，目标必须是唯一的，而且是你自己选的。

sentences.en: You cannot have competing goals.
sentences.zh: 你不能有互相竞争的目标。

sentences.en: That splits focus and doesn't lead to a point of view at all.
sentences.zh: 那会分散注意力，根本形成不了任何视角。

sentences.en: And it cannot be inherited from your parents, your culture, your industry or your algorithm.
sentences.zh: 而且它不能是从你父母、你的文化、你所在的行业或者你的算法那里继承来的。

sentences.en: So the finished version of setting this goal is when you can say, I do this with total conviction and you can instantly see that most of what you're currently doing has nothing to do with that goal.
sentences.zh: 所以，设定这个目标的完成版是，当你能说出"我做这件事，带着完全的信念"，并且你能立刻看到，你目前做的大部分事情都跟这个目标毫无关系。

sentences.en: And then I can also welcome you to the unknown, which is the most meaningful place to be.
sentences.zh: 然后，我也可以欢迎你进入未知，那是最有意义的地方。

sentences.en: Now, the second step is to set standards for what you don't do and stick to them.
sentences.zh: 第二步，为你"不做的事"设定标准，并且死守这些标准。

sentences.en: Now, this should already be a thing if the goal is properly set.
sentences.zh: 如果目标设定得当，这应该已经自然发生了。

sentences.en: But if the goal doesn't feel properly set, then you need to do this as well.
sentences.zh: 但如果目标感觉没设定对，那你也需要做这一步。

sentences.en: You need to define what you just don't do anymore.
sentences.zh: 你需要定义清楚，你从此不再做什么。

sentences.en: So you have to audit your life, every habit, every project, every client, every relationship, routine and obligation.
sentences.zh: 所以你必须审视你的生活，每一个习惯、每一个项目、每一个客户、每一段关系、日常惯例和义务。

sentences.en: Do any of them help you reach the goal?
sentences.zh: 它们中有任何一个能帮你达成目标吗？

sentences.en: The answer is almost certainly no. And this is the hardest part because you have to create a standard that you refuse to lower.
sentences.zh: 答案几乎肯定是不能。而这是最难的部分，因为你要创造一条你拒绝降低的标准。

sentences.en: And these are the things that you no longer do, period.
sentences.zh: 这些就是你不再做的事，句号。

sentences.en: You don't almost stop partying on the weekends or undercharging for your freelance services.
sentences.zh: 你不是"差不多不再周末去派对"或者"差不多不再低价接自由职业的单"。

sentences.en: You completely eliminate that behavior.
sentences.zh: 你是彻底消除那个行为。

sentences.en: And of course, this is easier said than done.
sentences.zh: 当然，这说起来容易做起来难。

sentences.en: There's the sunk cost bias like, oh, I've invested so much in this.
sentences.zh: 会有沉没成本偏见，比如"哦，我已经在这上面投入了这么多"。

sentences.en: It would just be irrational to stop doing it now or fear or just having a lack of accountability.
sentences.zh: 现在停下来太不理性了，或者是因为恐惧，或者就是缺乏问责。

sentences.en: And that's because the mind is a self-deception machine.
sentences.zh: 那是因为，大脑是一台自我欺骗的机器。

sentences.en: That's what the mind does best is it deceives you and it lies to you.
sentences.zh: 大脑最擅长的事，就是欺骗你，对你撒谎。

sentences.en: And humans just love lying to themselves so they can stay the same.
sentences.zh: 而人类就是喜欢对自己撒谎，这样他们就可以保持不变。

sentences.en: The best way to frame this, in my opinion, is as a chance to practice brutal self-honesty and just rip multiple band-aids off.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，最好的理解方式，是把它当作一个练习残酷的自我诚实的机会，然后一次性撕掉好几张创可贴。

sentences.en: So the finished version of raising your standards is that life feels dramatically simpler.
sentences.zh: 所以，拉高标准的完成版是，生活感觉变得极其简单。

sentences.en: You just have less weight on your shoulders.
sentences.zh: 你肩上的重量变轻了。

sentences.en: You have fewer things, fewer obligations and fewer justifications that clog your mind and prevent you from action.
sentences.zh: 你有更少的东西、更少的义务、更少的自我辩解，那些东西会堵塞你的大脑，阻止你行动。

sentences.en: Now, step three is to focus on the highest leverage path available to you because you have the goals.
sentences.zh: 第三步，专注于你能走的最高杠杆路径，因为你现在有了目标。

sentences.en: Now, what do you do?
sentences.zh: 那么，你该做什么？

sentences.en: And this may not come immediately.
sentences.zh: 而这可能不会立刻到来。

sentences.en: You probably have to experiment a little bit.
sentences.zh: 你可能需要稍微实验一下。

sentences.en: You just have to try things.
sentences.zh: 你只需要去尝试。

sentences.en: You have to learn and do until the path becomes clear because your goal has created a frame that allows you to notice new opportunities and your standards subtract everything from your life that does not serve the goal, which creates space for your attention to actually move in the right direction.
sentences.zh: 你必须边学边做，直到路径变得清晰，因为你的目标创造了一个框架，让你能注意到新的机会，而你的标准会把生活中一切无助于目标的东西都剔除出去，从而为你的注意力腾出空间，让它真正朝正确的方向移动。

sentences.en: So now you must accept that there are very few real paths to achieve the goal, but you don't find the path, person or opportunity fully formed for something like fitness, the delusional goal, which is again, impossible outcome plus impossible deadline is to compete in a physique show in six months or squat four or five for the first time this year.
sentences.zh: 所以现在你必须接受，实现目标的真正路径非常少，但你不是直接找到一条现成的路径、人或机会——比如健身，那个妄念目标，也就是不可能的结果加不可能的截止日期，是六个月后参加一场健美比赛，或者今年第一次深蹲四五百磅。

sentences.en: Like seriously, when was the last time you set a goal like this and actually pursued it?
sentences.zh: 说真的，你上一次设定这样的目标并真正去追求它，是什么时候？

sentences.en: Because for those who have set these types of goals, you understand that you look back on your life and you remember that point in your life.
sentences.zh: 因为对那些设定过这类目标的人来说，你明白，当你回望人生时，你会记住那个节点。

sentences.en: You don't remember anything else.
sentences.zh: 其他的你什么都不记得。

sentences.en: You don't remember the things you do every day that you love so much supposedly like playing video games and eating an entire pizza to yourself.
sentences.zh: 你不会记得那些你每天做、你自以为很爱的事情，比如打游戏、一个人吃掉一整张披萨。

sentences.en: Like you just don't remember that because that's your normal life.
sentences.zh: 你就是不记得那些，因为那是你的日常。

sentences.en: And as a tangent, it's just crazy how normal this is.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，这种日常有多普遍，简直离谱。

sentences.en: When I log on Instagram, I see this whole doomsday thing, like how Dune part three and Avengers doomsday are coming out at the same time.
sentences.zh: 我每次登录 Instagram，都能看到那种末日狂欢的东西，比如《沙丘3》和《复仇者联盟：末日》同时上映。

sentences.en: And so people have this schedule of, okay, we're going to watch Dune part three at 10 a.m. Then we're going to go to like McDonald's or Burger King or something.
sentences.zh: 于是人们就有了这样的日程：好，我们早上十点看《沙丘3》，然后去麦当劳或汉堡王什么的。

sentences.en: And then we're going to watch the Avengers at 7 p.m. And then we're going to play GTA six all night.
sentences.zh: 然后晚上七点看《复仇者联盟》，再然后通宵玩 GTA 6。

sentences.en: Now I get it.
sentences.zh: 我理解。

sentences.en: I'm going to watch those two movies, but how this goes viral every single time like that is the most shit and boring life that you could ever have.
sentences.zh: 我也会去看那两部电影，但这种事每次都能病毒式传播，仿佛那是你能拥有的最垃圾、最无聊的人生。

sentences.en: And as I said, I'm going to watch those movies.
sentences.zh: 我说了，我会去看那些电影。

sentences.en: I'm not going to play GTA six because I don't have a console.
sentences.zh: 我不会玩 GTA 6，因为我没有主机。

sentences.en: Like I don't even care to play it anymore.
sentences.zh: 我甚至已经不在乎玩不玩了。

sentences.en: It's genuinely not interesting to me.
sentences.zh: 它对我来说真的没意思。

sentences.en: And I'm not saying that as like an oh, I'm better.
sentences.zh: 我说这话不是那种“哦，我更高尚”的意思。

sentences.en: It's just not interesting to me.
sentences.zh: 就是单纯没意思。

sentences.en: But like every single day, like that's your lifestyle.
sentences.zh: 但每一天，这就是你的生活方式。

sentences.en: Every single day, something is wrong, terribly wrong.
sentences.zh: 每一天，都有问题，严重的问题。

sentences.en: One of my friends is in crypto, and I didn't believe him when he first said this, but he was telling me that like me building Eden wasn't the right move because he knows for a fact that the future is just moving towards three things.
sentences.zh: 我一个朋友是做加密货币的，他第一次说的时候我不信，但他告诉我，我构建 Eden 不是正确的选择，因为他确切地知道，未来只会朝三样东西发展。

sentences.en: Gambling, porn and video games.
sentences.zh: 赌博、色情和电子游戏。

sentences.en: That's it. And now I see that everywhere.
sentences.zh: 就这些。现在我到处都能看到这一点。

sentences.en: That's it. That's where the future is going.
sentences.zh: 就这些。那就是未来的走向。

sentences.en: That doesn't mean I'm going to stop building Eden because I do think there's still a shred of hope for people to want to create things.
sentences.zh: 这不意味着我会停止构建 Eden，因为我确实认为，人们想要创造东西的意愿，还有一丝希望。

sentences.en: But it's just absurd. It's absurd back.
sentences.zh: 但这太荒谬了。太荒谬了。

sentences.en: Well, let's get back to the video.
sentences.zh: 好了，我们回到视频。

sentences.en: So when you set this goal of a physique show in six months or squatting four or five, you have to watch what happens to your attention.
sentences.zh: 所以当你设定这样一个目标——六个月后参加健美比赛，或者深蹲四五百磅——你必须观察你的注意力会发生什么变化。

sentences.en: Suddenly, the linear path of show up, lift, repeat, that just doesn't work anymore.
sentences.zh: 突然间，那条线性的路径：出现、举铁、重复，不再管用了。

sentences.en: You need structure.
sentences.zh: 你需要结构。

sentences.en: You may need a coach who can get you on the right track fast.
sentences.zh: 你可能需要一个教练，能让你快速走上正轨。

sentences.en: Your current training program needs to solely focus on the sets, reps and exercises that will get you there.
sentences.zh: 你当前的训练计划，必须只聚焦在能让你达成目标的那些组数、次数和动作上。

sentences.en: You start seeing sleep and food as strict and non-negotiable.
sentences.zh: 你开始把睡眠和饮食看作严格且不可妥协的事。

sentences.en: All things that you didn't even think about because your previous goal filtered it out as noise.
sentences.zh: 所有这些事你以前根本不会去想，因为你之前的目标把它们当作噪音过滤掉了。

sentences.en: Now, when I wanted to hit my first 100K a month in business, which was a delusional goal for me, who is making under a little bit under 100K as a freelancer, I only had around a thousand followers on social media.
sentences.zh: 当我想在生意上达到第一个月入10万美元时，这对我来说是个妄想式的目标，我当时做自由职业者，收入还不到10万，社交媒体上只有一千个左右的粉丝。

sentences.en: And so that's kind of impossible, you would think.
sentences.zh: 所以你会觉得，这几乎不可能。

sentences.en: And so me posting content normally or trying to go on social media wasn't going to get me there in a short enough time frame.
sentences.zh: 我如果正常发内容，或者只是去社交媒体上试试，根本不可能在足够短的时间内达到那个目标。

sentences.en: I just obviously wasn't going to get there by posting consistently and hoping the algorithm notices me.
sentences.zh: 靠持续发帖、指望算法注意到我，显然是不可能达到的。

sentences.en: So I had to find leverage.
sentences.zh: 所以我必须找到杠杆。

sentences.en: I had to find force multipliers.
sentences.zh: 我必须找到力量倍增器。

sentences.en: I needed an offer first that would actually convert.
sentences.zh: 我首先需要一个真正能转化的产品。

sentences.en: That's a part of it.
sentences.zh: 这是其中一部分。

sentences.en: But I also needed more distribution than the thousand followers I had.
sentences.zh: 但我也需要比那一千个粉丝更大的分发渠道。

sentences.en: And so I could go the paid ads route, but I didn't have the money to invest enough into that and I just didn't know how to do it.
sentences.zh: 我可以走付费广告这条路，但我没有足够的钱去投入，而且我也不知道怎么做。

sentences.en: And so instead, a viable route was borrowing other people's audiences, meaning I had to network in exchange value with someone who had 20 or 50 or 100,000 followers that would share my post to their audience so that I would get a lot more traffic to my offer.
sentences.zh: 所以，另一条可行的路是借用别人的受众，也就是说，我必须去和有2万、5万或10万粉丝的人进行价值交换，让他们把我的帖子分享给他们的受众，这样我的产品就能获得更多流量。

sentences.en: And so we talk about multiple ways to do that in the creator boot camp, which is a part of the pro annual plan of Eden link in the description.
sentences.zh: 我们在创作者训练营里讲了很多种方法，这是Eden年度专业计划的一部分，链接在描述里。

sentences.en: But that's what a lot of people miss is they just follow the generic advice because they have generic goals.
sentences.zh: 但很多人忽略的就是这一点，他们只是遵循那些通用的建议，因为他们只有通用的目标。

sentences.en: And now if you don't know what Eden is, Eden is a second brain for creators where you can save any idea or anything from across the web, research what ideas are already working, create content people can't ignore and soon with the next update, get paid for your knowledge.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不知道Eden是什么，Eden是创作者的第二大脑，你可以保存任何想法或网上的任何东西，研究哪些想法已经奏效，创作人们无法忽视的内容，并且很快，随着下一次更新，你可以靠你的知识获得收入。

sentences.en: So it's going to be build a second brain and then monetize it or monetize your knowledge because everyone's talking about how info products are dead when I don't think that's the case.
sentences.zh: 所以它会是先构建第二大脑，然后把它变现，或者说把你的知识变现，因为所有人都在说信息产品已经死了，但我不这么认为。

sentences.en: I just don't think they've evolved into the age.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得它们还没有进化到这个时代。

sentences.en: And so that's what we're building.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们正在构建的东西。

sentences.en: And it's going to be frictionless to get your first product up because if you have any valuable thing that you do in a I'm going to make it so you can monetize that not by just sharing a prompt or a skill, but by actually getting paid for it.
sentences.zh: 而且它会让你毫无阻力地上架你的第一个产品，因为如果你做任何有价值的事，我会让你能把它变现，不只是分享一个提示词或一个技能，而是真正靠它获得收入。

sentences.en: I see that as the next wave of info products.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是信息产品的下一波浪潮。

sentences.en: They're just going to be a lot better and a lot more valuable to your customers.
sentences.zh: 它们会变得好得多，对你的客户有价值得多。

sentences.en: If you actually want to see that at minimum, you can just sign up for a free account and start playing around, start writing, start saving ideas, start taking notes.
sentences.zh: 如果你想至少看看这个，你可以直接注册一个免费账户，开始玩一玩，开始写作，开始保存想法，开始记笔记。

sentences.en: But then you'll get the email when the update goes live.
sentences.zh: 然后当更新上线时，你会收到邮件。

sentences.en: So now after all of this, everything we just talked about, now that your focus is singular, you're more disciplined than 99 percent of humanity.
sentences.zh: 所以，在这一切之后，在我们刚刚谈完的所有事情之后，现在你的专注力是单一的，你比99%的人更自律。

sentences.en: But you love it.
sentences.zh: 但你热爱它。

sentences.en: It is one of the greatest things you can experience on this planet.
sentences.zh: 这是你在这个星球上能体验到的最棒的事情之一。

sentences.en: And if you do not feel this joy, that's another problem.
sentences.zh: 如果你感受不到这种喜悦，那是另一个问题。

sentences.en: So in the next video, we're going to talk about how to add gravity to your goals and how discipline isn't something that you just brute force.
sentences.zh: 所以在下一个视频里，我们会讲如何为你的目标增加引力，以及自律不是靠蛮力硬撑出来的。

sentences.en: So if you want that video, subscribe, check the links in the description as mentioned, like the video while you're here and I'll see you in the next one.
sentences.zh: 如果你想看那个视频，请订阅，查看描述里的链接，顺便给这个视频点个赞，我们下个视频见。

sentences.en: Bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。
